How is Iowa organized when you sell a house?

Iowa has 99 counties, and almost every step of a home sale runs through a county office. Wikipedia's county list shows Polk County as the largest at 516,546 residents and Adams County as the smallest at 3,617, so the courthouse you deal with can be a big metro office or a very small one.

A city address does not always tell you the county. Des Moines sits in Polk and Warren counties, Urbandale in Polk and Dallas, West Des Moines in Polk, Dallas and Warren, and Sioux City in Woodbury and Plymouth, according to Wikipedia's list of Iowa cities. Check the parcel record before you call anyone.

Three county offices come up most often:

  • The county treasurer, who collects property tax and runs the annual tax sale.
  • The county recorder, who records deeds and takes the declaration of value.
  • The clerk of the district court, who handles estates and eviction filings.

Our county and city links are grouped below. For tax questions that apply across the state, start with our Iowa property tax guide, or browse Iowa guides by city and county.

When is Iowa property tax due, and when does it go delinquent?

Iowa property tax is paid in two installments, and each has its own delinquency date. Under Iowa Code 445.37, the first installment becomes delinquent on October 1 if it was not paid before then, and the second becomes delinquent on April 1. When the last day of September or March lands on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the following month.

To avoid interest, the same section says payment must reach the treasurer on or before the last business day of the month before the delinquent date, or carry a qualifying postmark. A payment dropped off on the 30th of September can already be late for interest purposes.

ItemWhat the statute says
First installment delinquentOctober 1, unless it falls on a weekend
Second installment delinquentApril 1, unless it falls on a weekend
Annual tax saleThird Monday in June, for parcels with delinquent taxes (Iowa Code 446.7)
Tax sale amountTaxes, interest, fees and costs due

A seller who is behind should talk to the county treasurer before June, because the tax sale offers delinquent parcels each year. Our Iowa tax deed and tax lien sales page walks through what follows a sale.

Does Iowa have a homestead exemption, and does it affect a sale?

Yes, and it changed in 2026. The Iowa Department of Revenue says Senate File 2472, signed May 18, 2026, replaces the homestead tax credit with an exemption equal to 10 percent of the home's taxable value.

  • The minimum exemption is $5,500 of taxable value and the maximum is $20,000.
  • The change is retroactive to assessment year 2026 and shows up on property taxes paid in September 2027 and March 2028.
  • After 2027 the Department adjusts the maximum for inflation.
  • The disabled veteran homestead tax credit is not eliminated.

For a seller, the practical point is that the exemption lowers the taxable value on an owner-occupied home, so a buyer's first bill may look different from yours. Details on eligibility are on our Iowa homestead exemption page.

What taxes and fees come with transferring a deed in Iowa?

Iowa charges a transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500, or fraction of $500, of consideration above the first $500. That rule is in Iowa Code 428A.1, which also says a transfer with no consideration owes no tax.

The same section requires a declaration of value, signed by at least one seller or buyer or an agent, when a deed goes to the county recorder. The recorder does not record the declaration. It goes to the assessor for sales ratio studies.

Consideration means the full actual sale price, including any lien or encumbrance the buyer assumes. Personal property listed separately on the deed can be subtracted.

QuestionAnswer from Iowa Code 428A.1
Transfer tax rate$0.80 per $500 above the first $500
Transfer with no considerationNo tax
Who signs the declarationA seller, a buyer, or their agent
Where it is filedCounty recorder where the land lies

Recording fees are set by the county, so call the recorder for the current schedule. Our Iowa quitclaim deed page covers the deed form side.

What happens when a seller faces a sheriff sale in Iowa?

After a property is sold at a sheriff sale, Iowa Code 628.3 lets the debtor redeem it at any time within one year from the day of sale. The debtor stays in possession during that year, and the first six months of the right to redeem belong only to the debtor.

A redeemed property comes back free of any liability for the unpaid part of the judgment it was sold under. That gives an owner time to sell the house, pay the debt from proceeds, and walk away without the judgment attached to the property.

We did not confirm the full pre-sale foreclosure timeline from an official page, so ask the clerk of the district court in your county or an Iowa attorney how a specific case stands. Our Iowa sheriff sale page covers the steps in more detail.

What should heirs know before selling an inherited house in Iowa?

Iowa no longer collects inheritance tax on recent deaths. The Department of Revenue states the tax is not applicable for deaths occurring on or after January 1, 2025.

The Department also says its information is not about probate and tells readers to contact an attorney with estate questions. Probate runs through the district court in the county where the estate is opened, and the county clerk of court is the office to call first.

Heirs who want to sell should confirm who has authority to sign, whether the house is titled in the decedent's name alone, and what liens are recorded. Our Iowa probate process and Iowa estate and inheritance tax pages give more background.

What are the rules when a rented house is being sold in Iowa?

A tenant's lease does not disappear because the owner wants to sell, so the landlord rules in Iowa Code chapter 562A still apply. Two notice periods in section 562A.27 matter most:

  • If rent is unpaid, the landlord can terminate the rental agreement when the tenant fails to pay within three days after written notice.
  • For other material noncompliance, the notice gives seven days to fix the problem, and the agreement ends if it is not fixed.

A tenant can raise defenses in a nonpayment case, such as the landlord's failure to meet repair duties under the code. Owners who plan to sell with a tenant in place should read the lease and keep notices in writing. See our Iowa landlord tenant law and Iowa eviction notice pages for more.

What does an as-is cash sale look like in Iowa?

An as-is cash sale means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and the seller does not repair or clean it first. It does not remove the seller's disclosure duties.

Iowa Code 558A.4 says the disclosure statement covers the condition and important characteristics of the property, including significant structural defects, under rules from the real estate commission. Those rules may also cover zoning, plumbing, heating, electrical systems and pests.

Before you list or accept any offer, gather these items:

  • Recent tax statements and any delinquent balance.
  • Payoff letters for each mortgage or lien.
  • Any lease for a tenant in the house.
  • Estate papers if the owner has died.

Cash Home Buyers works with owners dealing with inherited homes, back taxes, tenants and repairs. Request an offer from us at any stage, and ask the county office about anything above that depends on local practice, such as recording fees or the status of a delinquent parcel.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Iowa have?

Iowa has 99 counties. Polk is the most populous and Adams the least, according to Wikipedia's county list.

When do Iowa property taxes become delinquent?

The first installment is delinquent on October 1 and the second on April 1, with a weekend shift to the second business day. Interest cutoffs fall earlier, on the last business day of the prior month.

Does Iowa tax the transfer of a house?

Yes. Iowa Code 428A.1 sets 80 cents for each $500 of consideration above the first $500, and a declaration of value goes to the county recorder.

Can I redeem a house after a sheriff sale in Iowa?

The debtor can redeem within one year from the day of sale and keeps possession meanwhile, under Iowa Code 628.3.

Is there Iowa inheritance tax on a house inherited now?

The Department of Revenue says Iowa inheritance tax does not apply to deaths on or after January 1, 2025.

How much notice does an Iowa landlord give for unpaid rent?

A landlord may terminate if the tenant does not pay within three days after written notice, per Iowa Code 562A.27.

Does the Iowa homestead exemption change in 2026?

Yes. A 10 percent exemption replaces the credit, with a $5,500 minimum and $20,000 maximum of taxable value.

Who do I call about my county property tax?

Call the county treasurer. The recorder handles deeds, and the district court clerk handles estates.
